review_text_raw:
The game itself is good however there are some issues with it. First of all it is extremely short. I finished all cases in ~2.5 hours. [i](Edit: More cases were released delayed which added ~2hrs playtime)[/i]

There are some annoying bugs in the game such as the ingame notepad bugging out frequently, not letting you use arrowkeys for navigation, not letting you type over ~30% etc. Clicks on windows also click the windows and files underneath which is annoying. [i](edit: this got fixed)[/i]Trying to scroll in a certain window also scrolls all other scrollable windows(eg when scrolling through emails it will also scroll chats/websites and vice versa). 
There is no manual save, I had to restart cases twice even though I solved them because the game randomly decides not to autosave at any point. 
The arrest mechanic is also annoying. I have all the evidence needed to arrest someone yet somehow the game simply will not accept the evidence without any reason as to why. It is extremely picky and only wants the one piece that the dev marked as correct despite other files giving much more infos that would make much more sense. It's illogical a lot of times. 

The hacking mechanic is extremely basic. 99% of the hacking is typing iphack plus ip, then list then download all files. It would have been nice to see more hacking systems not just literally the same 2 super simplistic commands over and over. Worth a look at high discount. for me, overall disappointing and thus no recommendation.

review_text_raw:
Pretty boring, to be honest. It feels so much like a bootleg version of Hacknet, except without the badass soundtracks and cool hacking features.


[b]/STORY and CHARACTERS (6/10)/[/b]

First things first, let's start with the story and characters. You're an agent from the government cyber security agency MI7 that investigates with other MI7 agents a group of hackers called Thorn who breached their servers. Your job is to track down all the members of the group and arrest them for a different crime in order to hide the security breach to the public. Alright, sounds simple enough, but that's because it IS simple, it's not more fleshed out than that. You spend the whole game hunting down an entire hacker group, then find an excuse to arrest them (I'll get back on that later). Even when you detain the big leader, none of what you've done felt satisfying after that.

As for the characters, well you don't have that much of character development from them, except for the "smart girl of the team" agent Sharp, the "bossy boss who takes his job way too seriously" Osvalt, the "I prefer old TTS softwares" agent on the field Cooper, the "flirty secretary who puts winky emojis all over her emails" Ashley, the "hahaha, I'm evil" hacker group leader Mr. Blue. Anyway, you get the point. Each character is only limited to one main characteristic and that's it.

[b]/GAMEPLAY (4/10)/[/b]

Oh boy, the gameplay is the main(lining) reason why I'm not recommending this. Jeez, where do I start? Well, first of all, if you're expecting to feel like a hacker, you're in for a disappointment. All you get is a command-prompt application with two script-kiddie commands: one that gets a website's IP and one that hacks into someone's computer using the said IP. That's right, throughout the whole game you'll spend most of your time typing 'ping', 'iphack', 'ping', 'iphack' while searching a computer's files in a DOS-style file navigation system. The devs claimed that it was on purpose in order to emphasize the narration over actual hacking. I would be fine with that kind of decision, but that doesn't mean you should stick to that repetitive "look at a website, ping, iphack and read files" bulls hit. At least keep an enjoyable gameplay in the background as well. Luckily, you get some other apps (like the google map one) and Operating Systems on the way.

On top of that, the arrest system is really nitpicky about which evidence you use against the person. Each case has around three alternate crimes to choose from to arrest the person you're tracking. However, only 1 evidence per crime is accepted code-wise. In other words, if you choose a proof that totally makes sense but wasn't chosen by the devs, it doesn't count. I ended up spamming the "begin arrest" button with every file I snatched.

As for the OS interfaces, it's a buggy mess, no matter which one is it. You start off with a parody Windows XP, which is pretty nice. You also get parody Ubuntu, parody Mac and parody Windows Vista/7 on the way, which is also great. The pixel art is pretty good, but the Operating Systems look so limited in comparison to the real thing, they don't feel like Operating Systems that anyone would actually use in real life (I know it's just a game, but come on). You can't delete files in your folder (too bad if you accidentally downloaded the same thing twice!) and the notepad doesn't save what you wrote into a text file, which is pretty inconvenient when I constantly need to write down IPs and names (and if you accidentally closed the notepad, too bad!). Also, if you keep windows open in Windows XP, then switch to another OS, open windows in that said OS, then switch back to Windows XP, the windows will start overlapping. I'm not impressed, man. Don't you have a "visible/invisible" property on your images or something in the engine you're using? Oh, and you're gonna love this one: the program is so delayed that if you type something way too fast, some keys will be ignored. Most of the time, you're going to have a lot of "mainlining" ending up like "manliin" because the game couldn't keep track of everything you typed down. This is super annoying when you type an IP, but get an error because the fucking game missed a keystroke and you don't know why it doesn't work since the error message doesn't tell you anything about what went wrong.

There are even reports of people who couldn't advance in some cases because the program forgot to add certain chat messages on the left to let you continue, which is frustrating when you can't even save in the middle of a case and instead start the whole thing over again. Luckily, I didn't encounter those case advancement bugs, but if you can't make a OS interface themed game with basic typing and windows manipulation without being overflowed with bugs, you shouldn't even sell it at 8-10 bucks. Personally, from my experience with this game, I think it should be five dollars at best, or even free.

[b]/CONCLUSION/[/b]

To conclude, I don't recommend this game. It's half-baked, it looks like a prototype game and doesn't have any satisfaction upon playing it whatsoever. The replayability value is somewhat there, but I put the game aside about two or three times before finally finishing it. If you feel like buying a hacking game without caring about anything else, then go for it. Otherwise, I'm giving this game...

review_text_raw:
Solve cases by pseudo-hacking other people's accounts and look for contextual clues to the case at hand. Submit the suspect, location, and evidence pointing to the case to produce an arrest.

I just finished the 3rd case. I've had to look online for help in every case. This makes me think the game is poorly designed.

A few good ideas, but overall poor execution.

Good ideas
- I like the pixel art
- I enjoy the pseudo emulation of an older Operating System

Poor Execution
- there are seemingly several ways to try to convict a suspect, given the multitude of evidence pieces one can submit; however this quickly turns into trial-and-error. Given a suspect / location / evidence combination, you'll be graded right or wrong. Submitting a wrong answer does not produce a penalty. You end up submitting several combinations in order to solve the case. This becomes frustrating, as it's no longer a logic-based game, but one where you *think* you have it right, get it wrong, then submit all other logical combinations in frustration.

It's almost there, but not good enough for me to recommend.

review_text_raw:
I loved the idea of an interface-em'-up, and I'm going to keep plinking away at it later, but I just don't seem to like this game so far.  
     I know it's part of the aesthetic, but nothing fits on your monitor, leading to frustrating moments dragging things around to make enough space without closing something, as most of your screens cannot be resized or minimized. Additionally, sometimes when I had more than 2 windows open two of them would begin flickering wildly for some reason. Could chalk it up to intentional jank because of the old-style OS but it sure looked like a bug to me.
     Beyond that, there's a lot of weird things that have been left out in terms of usability: you cannot use the arrow keys to go back on a line of text, so you have to delete and retype if you make an error. Nor can you use the up key to go to a previously entered line of code in the command-line more than once.
    What this leads to is enough irritation in the first two cases (suppose I should have played the demo) that I am already going to set the game down until I have the patience to give it another shot, at which point if I can hack it through I'll update this review.
    I will say that the atmosphere provided is pretty nice. The gentle music in the background with the sounds of the street outside, combined with the hilariously exaggerated typing and clicking sounds that the game makes when you do those actions, well, it's kinda relaxing. There was a bit in case 2 where the music ramped up a bit, but it was while you're supposed to be watching someone drive around on google maps, and you have no agency, so I don't think it had the impact they were going for. Not on me anyhow.

review_text_raw:
While I enjoyed my first 3 hours of the game, I ran into a bug that first appeared to inhibit my progress in the game. While the bug seemed like a significant oversight in the development process, one bug is understandable and after doing an online search I determined that you could still complete the mission while the bug was being worked on.
What made Mainlining an utterly frustrating experience for me was receiving specific instruction in the game that were not correct. There is one mission in particular where your partner says you must provide a legal document to prove that someone had a name change. I did this and failed the mission.
On top of that (same mission), the suspect lived in one area, but had expressed that he was going to move back home with his parents in an email. When I tried arresting the subject in the area where his parents live, I failed the mission and was met with a message that said attempting to make an arrest in that area failed to produce a suspect. I then tried to make an arrest where the suspect stated he lived. I was met with another message that I failed the mission, but that the area I made the arrest produced the suspect. I thought to myself, okay, I now know this person lives in this area, but I must have the wrong evidence. This was a little frustrating already given that my AI partner said I had to provide legal evidence of a name change and that's the evidence I was presenting.
I then tried evidence after evidence, clicking through documents and trying them out in my arrest attempt with the same suspect in the area where he said he lived. I kept receiving fail messages. I thought, okay, maybe I completely missed a small detail and have the wrong suspect.
I reviewed each document in the mission and determined that either I'm totally missing something or I'm experiencing a serious progress bug. I finally quit the game and go online to find out the answer (,which can be a frustrating thing to have to do for a video game). I find out that I had the correct suspect and had the correct evidence at one point in my many attempts, but the location I was attempting the arrest in was incorrect and the suspect was actually in the area where his parents live.
I was incredibly frustrated with this given that the game not only was telling me in my failed attempts that searching for the suspect in the area where his parents live fails to produce a suspect, but also that the 'correct' evidence to produce was not what your AI partner told you to provide and was not even in the top 3 pieces of evidence that seemed like the logical choice. This poor communication in the instruction, misinformation, and seemingly inflexible choice to go about the arrest made for an all-around frustrating experience in an otherwise good game (minus the aforementioned bug I came across).
Given Steam's policy of not being able to play games after 2 hours of play, I was unable to refund the game. I certainly understand having such a policy in place and I'm not blaming the developers for this complaint, but it only adds frustration when you run into so many issues in a game that inhibit progress and point to poor design and oversight after only 3 hours of play. I love the aesthetic, premise, and mechanics of Mainlining, but my frustration with the game (and Steam) has lead me not to continue playing this game.

Lots of bugs

the interface often doesn't make sense. eg. logging into a bank account, at www.banksite.com you have to put www.banksite/accountnumber instead of www.banksite.com/accountnumber

the evidence you have to submit often doesn't make sense. eg. bank records that don't show any incriminating transactions or a text log with vague information instead of the actual hack file.

the suspects location that you have to submit often doesn't make sense. eg. in one case, everything says the suspect lives in one place but in the report you have to put his parents location to make the arrest.
one of the guides even has the correct but invalid (according to the game) location in the solution

there are multiple cases where you have evidence to make 3 different arrests but you can only choose one.

you can't go to websites using the IP, which you can in RL
you can't "iphack" using the URL instead of the IP, which you could if it was RL (IP and URL are the same thing eg. www.google.com = 172.217.25.174 you can ping either of these in CMD with the same result, and you can put either of these into a web browser and you get the same page)
you can't move the cursor in the text boxes to fix mistakes, you have to backspace all the way and retype
you cannot delete useless files after downloading them
you cannot save important files from one case to another
you cannot save the notepad or edit other than backspace, once you get to the last line of the notepad you are screwed because you cannot edit it or type anything else unless you backspace
you cannot save mid mission

the list goes on....
